title: Capacity-blocked chip-firing: sharp weighted bound and a live-set characterization
statement: Let a finite loopless directed multigraph have an absorbing sink, nonsink arcs strictly forward in a fixed vertex order, and every nonsink vertex reaching the sink. Let b(v) bound incoming multiplicity, m(u,v) <= b(v) for all u, and assume d(v) + b(v) <= C(v) + 1, equivalently C(v) >= d(v) + max_u m(u,v) - 1 when b is the maximum. Then capacity-blocked firing terminates and every reachable capacity-terminal state is the ordinary normal form of its initial state. The unit-edge hypothesis C(v) >= d(v) is the case b = 1. Conversely, if the arc relation contains a directed cycle then preservation fails at every capacity with C(v) >= d(v); the two cases partition the model. Over arbitrary digraphs and arbitrary capacities, writing Live v for outdegree v <= capacity v, transfer holds exactly when the live subgraph is well founded under the receiver-chasing relation LiveArc v u = Live u and Live v and mult u v > 0, satisfies outdegree v + mult u v <= capacity v + 1 on live arcs, and is closed under arcs out of live vertices. Well-foundedness is equivalent, under live-closure, to the absence of a filled-set obstruction, so the ordering half of the characterization is a proved equivalence and not a census observation.
resolves: CBMD-DYN-CAPACITY-FIRING-001 open successor: the named candidate C(v) >= d(v) + max_u m(u,v) - 1
verified: The weighted overflow lemma, preservation of terminal states, and the full weighted transfer theorem compile under Lean 4.35.0 with no sorry, admit, or axiom declaration in the source.

Observed axiom dependencies from actual #print axioms output are exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; weighted_overflow_forces_unstable depends only on propext and unit_case_capacity_admits on none.
Exact enumeration found no failure at the bound across 8364 systems at n<=3 with multiplicity <=3, and 4596 systems at n<=4 with multiplicity <=2.
A separately implemented checker verified the theorem's own conclusion, that every capacity-terminal state equals the ordinary normal form, over 96053 initial states with zero disagreements.

Sharpness: lowering the bound by one at a single receiver of incoming multiplicity at least two produced 1344 transfer failures at n<=3 and 7544 at n<=4, and 17682 terminal disagreements in the independent adverse control.
A positive control reproduces failure at C(v) = d(v): 936 systems at n<=3 and 4256 at n<=4.
The checks gate on the transfer property rather than on nonconfluence, after enumeration showed the smallest C=d failure is confluent with a single wrong normal form.

The cycle obstruction compiles: a directed cycle plus C(v) >= d(v) yields a capacity-terminal state that is not ordinarily stable, built from the capacities themselves and therefore surviving every enlargement.
A forward ordering provably excludes the cycle structure used by that obstruction (ordered_has_no_closed_set, axiom dependency propext alone).
The cycle obstruction witness is confirmed in all 27,440 tested cyclic graph and capacity pairs, and an exhaustive state sweep found no cyclic system preserving transfer at any slack from 0 to 4.

Sufficiency over arbitrary digraphs compiles: under the three live-set conditions an admissible capacity-terminal state is ordinarily stable; vertices outside the live set are permanently ordinarily stable and need no argument.
A single filled-set obstruction compiles and yields both the cycle failure and the live-to-dead failure as instances; liveToDeadFilledSet constructs the two-member case and depends on no axioms.

Exactness census: over 798,025 systems (n<=3, multiplicity<=2, unit sink arcs, every capacity in 0..d(v)+2) the three conditions agree with the exact transfer property in every case, with zero unsound and zero incomplete.

Minimality: dropping ordered-on-live makes the predicate wrong on 63,847 systems, dropping the bound on 4,998, and dropping live-closed on 393,192; no drop produces an incomplete predicate, so the conditions are independent.

Necessity of the bound is proved: violating it on a live arc yields an explicit capacity-terminal state that is not ordinarily stable, with the truncated-subtraction branch handled rather than assumed away.
Necessity of live-closure is proved via the two-member filled set, which depends on no axioms.
Ordering together with live-closure provably admit no filled-set obstruction at all (depends on propext alone), so the sufficient conditions are exactly strong enough to exclude the obstruction.

Sufficiency is proved without finiteness: wf_terminal_implies_ordinary_stable replaces the rank, the bound rank v < n, and the ordering hypothesis by well-foundedness of LiveArc, and wellFounded_of_rank derives that hypothesis from the 0.3.0 ones, so the earlier sufficiency theorem is now an instance.

The obstruction is constructed directly from failure of the hypothesis: filledSetOfNotWellFounded takes membership to be non-accessibility and the arc to another non-accessible vertex as successor, using no pigeonhole, no topological order and no finiteness; a non-live vertex is accessible for free, so the witness is live with no extra hypothesis.

wellFounded_iff_no_filled_set compiles both directions: under live-closure, LiveArc is well founded exactly when no FilledSet exists. not_wellFounded_of_live_cycle gives the direction necessity needs, from a closed cycle of live vertices.

An independent content check (verification/reference/equivalence.py) tests the two statements over the same 798,025-system box by methods not shared with characterize.py: Kahn peeling for well-foundedness, a greatest-fixpoint kernel for FilledSet existence, and direct simulation of the theorem's own conclusion rather than of TRANSFER. Result: 119,251 systems satisfy the hypotheses, with 0 unsound and 0 incomplete.

The same check confirms a prediction of the revision rather than a statistic: well-foundedness failing forces the conclusion to fail, in all 260,172 such systems, with zero exceptions; an exception would refute the revision.

Anti-vacuity: well-foundedness alone is insufficient in 418,602 systems, live-closure is load-bearing for the equivalence in 413,604 systems outside it, and replacing each of the three hypotheses by True in turn produces unsoundness in every case.

At a receiver fed by a live sender along a unit arc, the bound is exactly capacity v >= outdegree v in both directions: sufficient by the transfer theorem and necessary by bound_necessary_at_unit_arc, an instance of bound_violation_defeats_transfer at multiplicity one that does not require the receiver to be live. The item listing this as unresolved had been settled since revision 0.4.0.

Non-absorbing sinks settled negatively (revision 0.7.0): with the sink capacitated at any finite level, the all-full state is capacity-terminal and, given a live vertex, not ordinarily stable, so transfer holds exactly when no vertex is live (capped_sink_breaks_transfer, no_live_all_stable). A gated census at sink capacities 0, 1, 2, 4 and n <= 3 agrees in all 1,789,740 cases with zero disagreements, checks the all-full witness directly on every live system, and finds 17,594 systems that transfer with the absorbing sink but fail at every finite cap.

The last imported fact is compiled (revision 0.8.0): a finite acyclic relation is well founded (wellFounded_of_acyclic, by counting ancestors over Fin n), and with the converse acyclic_of_wellFounded this gives liveArc_wellFounded_iff_acyclic, so the census's cycle detection provably decides the ordering hypothesis.
unresolved: novelty assessment and external specialist review
nonclaims: not a novelty determination; the capacity rule is classical finite-capacity Petri-net semantics and the ordinary chip-firing theory is classical and assumed
not an external independent verification; the second implementation is separately written but not externally authored
finite enumeration corroborates the theorem and does not prove it
ordinary well-foundedness and uniqueness enter as explicit hypotheses and are not proved here
the cycle obstruction assumes every vertex has positive outdegree and says nothing about capacities below d(v)
the ordering half of the characterization is now a proved equivalence; the exactness of the full three-condition predicate over the enumerated box remains a finite census result
Classical.choice is genuinely used to build the obstruction's successor map and is not eliminated

the cycle obstruction is the Petri-net-side form of a known queueing result: Liebeherr and Akyildiz give a necessary and sufficient deadlock-freedom condition over buffer cycles for closed networks under blocking-after-service, and no novelty is claimed for it
the live-set obstruction is a trap in the net, dually a siphon in the complemented net, and the two enabledness notions are Murata's strict and weak transition rules; both are classical objects
the capacitated-sink result says nothing about leaking or draining sinks, which are different models
smallest_decisive_test: Exhibit an ordered multigraph satisfying d(v) + max_u m(u,v) <= C(v) + 1 with a reachable capacity-terminal state that is not the ordinary normal form of its initial state; or a reference proving the same preservation statement with an explicit semantic translation.
